court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Philip J. vs Ashapura Minechem Ltd. And Anr
facts_of_case: Petitioner seeking quashing of FIR No. 35 of 2011 registered at Shrivardhan Police Station, Dist. Raigad, for offences under Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC), as also the charge-sheet filed therein on 3rd March 2014 before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Shrivardhan.

legal_principles.principle: Same set of facts can give rise to civil and criminal cases.
legal_principles.held: What is required is that an analysis of the material on record indicates at least prima facie ingredients of the offences registered against the accused.
cited_cases: Delhi Race Club (1940) Limited & Ors. Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr., (2024) 10 SCC 690

legal_principles.principle: Two offences of Sections 406 and 420 of the IPC cannot go together.
legal_principles.held: The offences under Sections 406 and 420 of the IPC cannot go together and at least one of them deserves to be knocked out.
cited_cases: Delhi Race Club (1940) Limited & Ors. Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr., (2024) 10 SCC 690

outcome.final_order: Interim stay of further proceedings was granted.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for quashing of FIR
preparing a case for cheque bounce dispute
